question: A woman who is exclusively breastfeeding her 4-week-old infant requests contraception. She has no other medical conditions. According to WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC), which is the CORRECT classification for combined oestrogen-progestogen oral contraceptive pills (COCs)?

answers.text: WHO MEC Category 1 — no restriction, COC can be initiated immediately

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: WHO MEC Category 1 means no restrictions. COCs are NOT Category 1 in early breastfeeding — oestrogen reduces milk volume and transfers to the infant, which are significant concerns.

answers.text: WHO MEC Category 2 — advantages generally outweigh risks, use with caution

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Category 2 applies to COC use in breastfeeding women at 6 weeks–6 months. Before 6 weeks postpartum, the classification is higher (Category 4) due to greater milk suppression risk and neonatal oestrogen exposure.

answers.text: WHO MEC Category 4 — unacceptable health risk, COC is contraindicated

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. COCs are WHO MEC Category 4 (contraindicated) for breastfeeding women less than 6 weeks postpartum. Oestrogen suppresses prolactin, reducing milk supply at a critical time for establishing lactation, and is excreted in breast milk potentially affecting the neonate.

answers.text: WHO MEC Category 3 — risks generally outweigh benefits, but COC may be considered if alternatives are unacceptable

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Category 3 applies to COCs during weeks 6–6 months of breastfeeding. At 4 weeks postpartum (before 6 weeks), this woman is in the Category 4 window — COC is contraindicated, not merely cautioned.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the WHO MEC framework: COCs before 6 weeks in a breastfeeding woman = Category 4 (contraindicated). After 6 weeks: Category 3 (<6 months) or Category 2 (>6 months). Progestogen-only methods are preferred.
Correct. COCs are WHO MEC Category 4 before 6 weeks postpartum in breastfeeding women. Progestogen-only pills (POP) are Category 2 and are the preferred hormonal option.
